newsitem.title: INDIA: Kashmiri separatists reject talks with state.
newsitem.headline: Kashmiri separatists reject talks with state.

text.p: Kashmiri separatists on Friday rejected an offer to hold talks with the National Conference party, which swept local assembly elections in India's Jammu and Kashmir state.

"We outright reject this offer," said Gulam Nabi Sumji, acting chairman of the All Parties Hurriyat (Freedom) Conference, which includes some 30 separatist groups. He was talking to reporters in the state's summer capital Srinagar.

On Wednesday, National Conference chief Farooq Abdullah told Reuters in an interview in the Indian capital that he was ready to hold talks with separatist leaders, who had urged voters to boycott last month's polls.
"How can we talk to Farooq Abdullah, who is at the mercy of New Delhi?" Sumji said.

Abdullah's party won a resounding majority in the state's 87-seat assembly in the first local elections since a separatist rebellion erupted in 1990. Abdullah has said he would like his party to join Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's United Front coalition in New Delhi.
"Abdullah's government will be a puppet regime of the Indian government," Sumji said. "We outright reject the election results."
